record.paper_title: Combinatorial properties of continuous graphs: A survey of challenges, solutions and open problems
record.context_brief: chromatic number of complete continuous graphs
record.original_question: For the complete graph K_n, let Γ(K_n) be its continuous counterpart and let χ_{1/2}(Γ(K_n)) denote the minimum number of colors needed in a (1/2, c)-coloring, meaning a cover of Γ(K_n) by radius-1/2 balls together with a coloring of those balls such that intersecting balls receive different colors. What is the exact value of χ_{1/2}(Γ(K_n)) as a function of n? The paper conjectures that χ_{1/2}(Γ(K_n)) = ⌈n/2⌉.

evidence.quote: Definition 11. Graph Γ is (r, c)-colourable if there is a set of balls B = {B(p, r) : p ∈ E} forming an r-cover of Γ and an assignment f : B → {1, . . . , c} such that for every two balls B, B′ ∈ B having non-empty intersection, i.e. B ∩ B′ ≠ ∅, it holds that f(B) ≠ f(B′). The r-chromatic number of Γ, further denoted by χr(Γ) or χr for simplicity, is the minimum number of colours c such that Γ is (r, c)-colourable.
A seemingly simple question to ask is: What is the 1/2-chromatic number of Γ(Kn)? ... We conjecture that the 1/2-chromatic number of Γ(Kn) is ⌈n/2⌉.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K_n$ denote the complete graph on $n$ vertices, with vertex set $\{v_1,\dots,v_n\}$ and an edge between every pair of distinct vertices. The continuous counterpart $\Gamma(K_n)$ is the topological realization of $K_n$ obtained by representing each edge as a unit-length copy of the closed interval $[0,1]$ and gluing endpoints according to the incidences in $K_n$. Equip $\Gamma(K_n)$ with the intrinsic shortest-path metric $d$, in which distance along each edge agrees with the standard distance on $[0,1]$. For a point $p\in\Gamma(K_n)$ and a real number $r>0$, let $B(p,r)=\{x\in\Gamma(K_n):d(x,p)\le r\}$ denote the closed ball of radius $r$.

For real numbers $r>0$ and a positive integer $c$, say that $\Gamma(K_n)$ is $(r,c)$-colourable if there exist a set $E\subseteq\Gamma(K_n)$ and a family of balls $\mathcal{B}=\{B(p,r):p\in E\}$ such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item $\bigcup_{B\in\mathcal{B}} B = \Gamma(K_n)$ (i.e.\ $\mathcal{B}$ is an $r$-cover of $\Gamma(K_n)$); and
\item there exists an assignment $f:\mathcal{B}\to\{1,2,\dots,c\}$ such that whenever two balls $B,B'\in\mathcal{B}$ satisfy $B\cap B'\neq\emptyset$, one has $f(B)\neq f(B')$.
\end{itemize}
The $r$-chromatic number $\chi_r(\Gamma(K_n))$ is the minimum $c$ for which $\Gamma(K_n)$ is $(r,c)$-colourable.

Determine $\chi_{1/2}(\Gamma(K_n))$ exactly as a function of $n$. In particular, decide whether
$$\chi_{1/2}(\Gamma(K_n)) = \left\lceil \tfrac{n}{2} \right\rceil$$
holds for every integer $n\ge 2$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a conjecture in a recent survey on combinatorial properties of continuous graphs. A web search did not surface any preprint or paper resolving the conjectured formula $\chi_{1/2}(\Gamma(K_n))=\lceil n/2\rceil$, so the problem appears to remain open.
